title: Inseparable Verbs
sourceNote: Transcript is auto-captioned and some German words were garbled (for example 'entlehren' is really 'entleeren', 'fair' is 'ver-'). All German here is reconstructed.
objectives: I can explain the difference between separable and inseparable verbs
I can use inseparable verbs in statements, questions and with modal verbs
I can conjugate verbs like verstehen
I know the inseparable prefixes be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, miss-, ver-, zer-

vocab.en: to chop up, to cut small

expressions.en: What do you recommend to me today?

grammar.title: Separable or inseparable?
grammar.body:
Some verbs have a prefix. With **separable** verbs (*aufstehen*) the prefix splits off and goes to the end of the sentence. With **inseparable** verbs (*verstehen*, **untrennbare Verben**) the prefix **never** separates; the verb stays in one piece.

Stress is a clue: in separable verbs the stress is **on the prefix** (*AUF-stehen*); in inseparable verbs the stress is **not on the prefix** (*ver-STE-hen*).
grammar.ar: الأفعال غير المنفصلة: البادئة لا تنفصل أبدًا ولا يقع عليها التشديد.

grammar.title: Word order
grammar.body: An inseparable verb behaves like any normal verb: **position 2** in statements and W-questions, **position 1** in yes/no questions. With a modal verb, the modal is in position 2 and the inseparable verb goes to the **end in the infinitive**.

grammar.title: Conjugation
grammar.body: Because the prefix does not separate, conjugation is easy: conjugate the verb as usual (regular or irregular). Irregular ones keep their vowel change, e.g. *empfangen* becomes *er empfängt*, *gefallen* becomes *es gefällt*.

grammar.title: Common inseparable prefixes
grammar.body: The prefixes **be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, miss-, ver-, zer-** are always inseparable. When you meet a new verb with one of them, treat it as inseparable.

head: Prefix
Verb
Example
rows: Wir bekommen bald eine neue Lehrerin.
Der Schulleiter empfängt seine Gäste herzlich.
Mein Sohn entdeckt jeden Tag etwas Neues.
Am Montag müssen wir die Mülltonne entleeren.
Kannst du mich auf diesem Foto erkennen?
Tom kann nie mein Vertrauen missbrauchen.
Im Unterricht kann man die Anweisungen manchmal missverstehen.
Wenn ich Schach spiele, verliere ich immer.
Ein Erdbeben kann manchmal viele Häuser zerstören.

grammar.title: Gehören and gefallen take the Dativ
grammar.body: The verbs *gehören* and *gefallen* are dative verbs: the person is in the Dativ (*mir, dir, ihm ...*). *Die Uhr gehört **mir**.* *Das Haus gefällt **mir**.*

mistakes.why: *verstehen* is inseparable; the prefix stays attached.
After a modal verb the main verb is an infinitive at the end.
*verkaufen* is inseparable; never send *ver-* to the end.

pronunciation.tip: Separable: stress on the prefix (*AUF-stehen*). Inseparable: no stress on the prefix (*ver-STE-hen*, *be-ZAH-len*).

lines.de: Herr Ober, was empfehlen Sie mir heute?
lines.en: Waiter, what do you recommend to me today?

lines.de: Gut. Kann ich mit Karte bezahlen?
lines.en: Good. Can I pay by card?

tip: Whenever you meet a new verb, try to use it in your own sentence and decide: is the prefix one of be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, miss-, ver-, zer-? Then it is inseparable.

comprehension.q: What does an inseparable verb do with its prefix?
comprehension.a: The prefix never separates from the verb.

comprehension.q: Where is the stress in a separable verb?
Where does the inseparable verb go when there is a modal verb?
comprehension.a: To the end of the sentence, in the infinitive.
For example be-, ver-, zer-, er-, ent-, emp-, ge-, miss-.

summary: Inseparable verbs (untrennbare Verben) keep their prefix attached in every position.
Typical prefixes: be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, miss-, ver-, zer-.
They follow normal word order: position 2 in statements, position 1 in yes/no questions, infinitive at the end after a modal verb.
Conjugate them like any verb: ich verstehe, du verstehst, er versteht ...
gehören and gefallen use the Dativ.
